# google_apihub_attribute

An attribute in the API Hub. An attribute is a name value pair which can be attached to different
resources in the API hub based on the scope of the attribute. Attributes can either be pre-defined
by the API Hub or created by users.


To get more information about Attribute, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/reference/apis/apihub/rest/v1/projects.locations.attributes)
* How-to Guides
    * [Create and manage API Hub attributes](https://cloud.google.com/apigee/docs/api-hub/manage-attributes)

## Example Usage - Apihub Attribute Basic


```hcl
resource "google_apihub_attribute" "attribute" {
  location     = "us-central1"
  attribute_id = "test-attribute"
  display_name = "Test Attribute"
  scope        = "API"
  data_type    = "STRING"
}
```
## Example Usage - Apihub Attribute Full


```hcl
resource "google_apihub_attribute" "attribute" {
  location     = "us-central1"
  attribute_id = "test-attribute-full"
  display_name = "Test Attribute Full"
  description  = "A comprehensive test attribute with all fields"
  scope        = "API"
  data_type    = "ENUM"
  cardinality  = 3
  
  allowed_values {
    id           = "production"
    display_name = "Production"
    description  = "Production environment"
  }
  
  allowed_values {
    id           = "staging"
    display_name = "Staging"
    description  = "Staging environment"
  }
  
  allowed_values {
    id           = "development"
    display_name = "Development"
    description  = "Development environment"
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  Required. The display name of the attribute.

* `scope` -
  (Required)
  Required. The scope of the attribute. It represents the resource in the
  API Hub to which the attribute can be linked.
  Possible values are: `SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED`, `API`, `VERSION`, `SPEC`, `API_OPERATION`, `DEPLOYMENT`, `DEPENDENCY`, `DEFINITION`, `EXTERNAL_API`, `PLUGIN`.

* `data_type` -
  (Required)
  Required. The type of the data of the attribute.
  Possible values are: `DATA_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED`, `ENUM`, `JSON`, `STRING`, `URI`.

* `location` -
  (Required)
  The location of the API Hub instance. This field is used to identify the
  location of the API Hub instance in which to create the attribute.


* `description` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. The description of the attribute.

* `allowed_values` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. The list of allowed values when the attribute value is of type enum.
  This is required when the dataType of the attribute is ENUM. The maximum number
  of allowed values of an attribute will be 1000.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_allowed_values).

* `cardinality` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. The maximum number of values that the attribute can have when
  associated with an API Hub resource. Cardinality 1 would represent a
  single-valued attribute. It must not be less than 1 or greater than 20.
  If not specified, the cardinality would be set to 1 by default and
  represent a single-valued attribute.

* `attribute_id` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. The ID to use for the attribute, which will become the final component
  of the attribute's resource name. This field is optional.
  * If provided, the same will be used. The service will throw an error if
  the specified id is already used by another attribute resource in the API hub.
  * If not provided, a system generated id will be used.
  This value should be 4-500 characters, and valid characters are /[a-z][A-Z][0-9]-_/.

* `project` - (Optional) The ID of the project in which the resource belongs.
    If it is not provided, the provider project is used.



<a name="nested_allowed_values"></a>The `allowed_values` block supports:

* `id` -
  (Required)
  The ID of the allowed value.

* `display_name` -
  (Required)
  The display name of the allowed value.

* `description` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. The description of the allowed value.

* `immutable` -
  (Optional)
  Optional. When set to true, the allowed value cannot be updated or deleted
  by the user. It can only be true for System defined attributes.

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/attributes/{{attribute_id}}`

* `name` -
  Identifier. The name of the attribute in the API Hub.
  Format: projects/{project}/locations/{location}/attributes/{attribute}

* `definition_type` -
  Output only. The definition type of the attribute.

* `mandatory` -
  Output only. When mandatory is true, the attribute is mandatory for the
  resource specified in the scope. Only System defined attributes can be mandatory.

* `create_time` -
  Output only. The time at which the attribute was created.

* `update_time` -
  Output only. The time at which the attribute was last updated.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 20 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 20 minutes.

## Import


Attribute can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/attributes/{{attribute_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{location}}/{{attribute_id}}`
* `{{location}}/{{attribute_id}}`


In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import Attribute using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/attributes/{{attribute_id}}"
  to = google_apihub_attribute.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), Attribute can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_apihub_attribute.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{location}}/attributes/{{attribute_id}}
$ terraform import google_apihub_attribute.default {{project}}/{{location}}/{{attribute_id}}
$ terraform import google_apihub_attribute.default {{location}}/{{attribute_id}}
```
